name: Hesperian-Counterscarp
description: Sand owns this world, in colors from bone-white to burnt sienna, migrating with the seasons before a patient wind. Where the gusts strip it away, a binary sunset emerge like the bones of the planet.

Breathable air makes every breath a small transaction. Locals, when there are locals, move slowly and speak quietly, conserving everything. Fossil beds suggest rich seas once flourished here; now the chemistry records only a slow suffocation.

The terrain around the starship crash site (colony ship) is scarred for kilometers, and the wreck's black box still loops two seconds of static on an obsolete band. Insurance investigators consider it a haunted assignment.
Survey contracts pay double for reasons nobody writes down. Veterans read the fine print, then read the survivors.
